title: Next steps in AI coding
author: emperormarkus
selftext:
I have been using AI for the last fist months to code home brew games.

I started with Python and made text-based games. I moved on to making games in HTML5. I like the fact you can play in browser and have one game file.

But, of course, there are serious limitations in terms of the overall quality of games you can make.

What format and code would you suggest I use next? I have been using more ancillary programs to make my games more interesting, such as adding better music using Sono, for example, and adding game prologues with dialogue using Elevenlabs.

Would love some ideas.

replies.author: AdStreet4350
replies.body: Get back rate some boobs brother

replies.author: mallcopsarebastards
replies.body: it's going to suck so much in 5 years when every job posting has knowing how to use AI tools as a requirement, and all the anti-AI radicals can't find jobs. It happened to admin roles a few short decades ago when every job posting started having word processing / email / spreadsheets, etc. We seem to have forgot how much of a problem that was for so many people.

replies.author: emperormarkus
replies.body:
I agree with you. I don’t get the hate. Some sort of weird purism verging on being a Luddite.

If someone is genuine coder then that’s awesome. But for the rest of us AI opened doors to creative things never possible before.

In the last year, I have published a novel, made two boardgames and over twenty games in a way that would never be possible before.

I use AI at work. I use AI as a better form of Google in my home life. So why not for games.

I am transparent about it.

comments.author: livercake
comments.body: try making a Pico8 game now, it's very streamlined and meant to be approachable

comments.author: emperormarkus
comments.body: Thanks - will take a look at this.

comments.author: TheFlamiingo
comments.body:
Tu peux faire beaucoup de chose, il faut juste bien préparer ta stack technique, et structurer ton projet de la bonne manière. 

Personnellement je travaille sur un MMORPG 2D en Web, j'utilise PixiJS V8 et WebGL/WebGPU pour le rendu graphique, et la partie serveur Colyseus. Tout ça en TypeScript.

Et mon projet avance bien, avec seulement des bases en développement. (Logique & méthodologie)

Il faut rechercher, prendre son temps, et comprendre ce que tu fais. L'IA est un outil de support qui va te faire gagner du temps, si elle n'est pas bien manager, ça ne marchera pas 

Donc à voir ce que tu veux faire exactement \^\^

replies.author: emperormarkus
replies.body:
I don’t at all disagree with that. I recognize that AI is a short cut for sure and you will never make something as good as what is commercially available.

Will take a look at what you suggest. I would love to find a way to improve the graphics on what I make.

replies.author: TheFlamiingo
replies.body: Quel type de graphisme ? Est-ce que tu parle d'interface ou de playermodel/environnement ?

replies.author: emperormarkus
replies.body: I am pretty good on the interfaces. I make clear title screens and cover images, for example. It is the overall look of the player features. I still use game sprites and know there are much better looks to be had.

comments.author: sannleikur
comments.body: If you're attached to the single-file browser thing, you could also push HTML5 further with a framework like phaser before jumping engines. Since you're already layering in ElevenLabs and Suno, running your sprite/art through Magnific keeps the visuals from being the weak link.

replies.author: emperormarkus
replies.body: Thanks - that’s helpful. Will check out Magnific. It would be nice to just improve some of the graphics a little.
